I will do it mostly the way I did before, because 4.1 mu is not big and every bag of fertilizer is real money. Around here in Quzhou, if wheat and maize look weak because I tried to save too much fertilizer, that loss hurts more than wasting a little. So I will follow what works on nearby fields with well water. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put the main fertilizer in before sowing, give one more nitrogen topdressing when it starts standing up strong after winter, and irrigate about 3 times if the water is normal. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, put some compound fertilizer at planting, then chase nitrogen around the big-leaf stage, and water about 2 times with the well if rain is not enough. I will use rotary tillage because it is cheaper and faster on my small land than deep ploughing every time. I will spray when I see real pest or weed pressure, usually 2 times on wheat and 2 times on maize. I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because I would rather spend a bit more than watch yield fall.
